speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing significant systemic symptoms, including night sweats, weight loss, and an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have had any recent unexplained fevers or if you have noticed any changes in your appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall experiencing any unintentional fevers above 38°C (100.4°F) in the past month? Additionally, have you noticed any skin itching or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the fixed supraclavicular lymph node and significant weight loss, I need to rule out malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT Scan of the Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the widespread lymphadenopathy and B symptoms, I need to confirm the cellular pathology. REQUEST TEST: Lymph Node Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms a B-cell lymphoma given the CD20 positivity. I need to know if you have experienced any alcohol-induced pain in your lymph nodes or noticed any skin lesions, as this helps distinguish between subtypes.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal fullness and tightness suggest significant splenomegaly or bulky abdominal disease, which is common in aggressive B-cell lymphomas. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
